claim: Cervical cancer is the fourth leading cause of cancer-related death among all types of women malignancies.
source: Cervical cancer (CC) is the fourth leading cause of cancer-related death among all types of women malignancies (Sung et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sung et al., 2021.

claim: Squamous cell carcinoma accounts for 70% of all cervical cancer cases.
source: The two major histological types of CC are squamous cell carcinoma of cervix (SCC) and adenocarcinoma of cervix (ADC), accounting for 70% and 25% of all cases, respectively (Cohen et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cohen et al., 2019.

claim: Adenocarcinoma accounts for 25% of all cervical cancer cases.
source: The two major histological types of CC are squamous cell carcinoma of cervix (SCC) and adenocarcinoma of cervix (ADC), accounting for 70% and 25% of all cases, respectively (Cohen et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cohen et al., 2019.

claim: ADC patients have a higher rate of rapid progression compared to SCC patients.
source: Compared to SCC, ADC patients have a higher rate of rapid progression, relapse, and insensitivity to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and even immunotherapy.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text.

claim: ADC patients have a higher rate of relapse compared to SCC patients.
source: Compared to SCC, ADC patients have a higher rate of rapid progression, relapse, and insensitivity to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and even immunotherapy.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text.

claim: ADC patients have insensitivity to chemotherapy compared to SCC patients.
source: Compared to SCC, ADC patients have a higher rate of rapid progression, relapse, and insensitivity to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and even immunotherapy.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text.

claim: ADC patients have insensitivity to radiotherapy compared to SCC patients.
source: Compared to SCC, ADC patients have a higher rate of rapid progression, relapse, and insensitivity to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and even immunotherapy.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text.

claim: ADC patients have insensitivity to immunotherapy compared to SCC patients.
source: Compared to SCC, ADC patients have a higher rate of rapid progression, relapse, and insensitivity to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and even immunotherapy.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text.

claim: ADC is considered a more aggressive phenotype than SCC.
source: Therefore, ADC is considered a more aggressive phenotype than SCC (Sasieni et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sasieni et al., 2009.

claim: Over 10% of early-stage cervical cancer patients are upstaged due to lymph node metastasis discovered after surgery.
source: Over 10% of patients, who are initially diagnosed with early stage and deemed suitable for radical surgery, end up being upstaged due to lymph node (LN) metastasis discovered after the surgery (Dabi et al., 2018; Thelissen et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dabi et al., 2018 and Thelissen et al., 2022.

claim: Misdiagnosed cervical cancer patients require additional radiotherapy after surgery according to NCCN guidelines.
source: According to the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines, these misdiagnosed patients require additional radiotherapy after surgery, even though they have underwent surgery (Bhatla et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bhatla et al., 2018.

claim: Combo treatment of surgery and radiotherapy may cause additional complications without offering more benefits than radiotherapy alone.
source: However, combo treatment of surgery and radiotherapy may cause additional complications and heavier financial burdens, without offering more benefits than radiotherapy alone (Cushman et al., 2018; Kashima et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cushman et al., 2018 and Kashima et al., 2023.

claim: CT or MRI can only detect suspiciously metastatic lymph nodes when the minimum diameter is ≥10 mm.
source: Unfortunately, radiological imaging tools do have limitations since CT or MRI can only detect suspiciously metastatic LN when the minimum diameter is ≥10 mm (Saleh et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Saleh et al., 2020.

claim: Persistent infection with human papillomavirus is the primary cause of cervical cancer.
source: Persistent infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary cause of CC (Mann et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mann et al., 2023.

claim: About 5–15% of cervical cancer patients test negative for HPV.
source: However, there are about 5–15% of patients testing negative for HPV (Yang et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2023.

claim: HPV-negative cervical cancer patients tend to experience worse clinical outcomes.
source: It is reported that HPV-negative patients tend to experience worse clinical outcomes (Fernandes et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fernandes et al., 2022.

claim: 30–50% of cervical cancer patients exhibit positive PD-L1 expression.
source: In CC, while it has been reported that 30–50% of patients exhibit positive PD-L1 expression, however, only an estimated 20–30% are expected to respond positively to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade therapy (Omenai et al., 2022; Sun et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Omenai et al., 2022 and Sun et al., 2020.

claim: Only an estimated 20–30% of cervical cancer patients are expected to respond positively to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade therapy.
source: In CC, while it has been reported that 30–50% of patients exhibit positive PD-L1 expression, however, only an estimated 20–30% are expected to respond positively to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade therapy (Omenai et al., 2022; Sun et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Omenai et al., 2022 and Sun et al., 2020.

claim: ADC is characterized as an immune-insensitive cancer type due to atypical modulation of the tumor immune microenvironment.
source: Therefore, CC, especially the pathological type of ADC, is characterized as an immune-insensitive cancer type due to atypical modulation of the TIME (Cao et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cao et al., 2023.

claim: The study performed single-cell RNA sequencing on 11 ADC samples and 4 SCC samples.
source: In the current study, we focused on the remodeling of TIME in ADC and performed scRNA-seq analysis on 11 ADC samples, with another 4 SCC samples included as controls.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing the study design.

claim: A total of 102,012 qualified cells were utilized for analysis.
source: The cell viability and sample quality were ensured beforehand, and a total of 102,012 qualified cells were utilized for further analysis (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 1A.

claim: The obtained cells were primarily categorized into 12 cell clusters.
source: The obtained cells were primarily categorized into 12 cell clusters, which were further re-clustered into 9 distinct cell types, based on specific gene markers (Li et al., 2022; Figure 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 1B and C.

claim: T cells comprised 38,627 cells in total, proportioning 37.87%.
source: These cell types included T cells (38,627 cells in total, proportioning 37.87%, marked with PTPRC, CD3D, CD3E, and CD3G)
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing cell type composition.

claim: Epithelial cells comprised 32,199 cells in total, proportioning 31.56%.
source: epithelial cells (32,199 cells in total, proportioning 31.56%, marked with EPCAM, SLP1, and CD24)
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing cell type composition.

claim: Neutrophils comprised 12,586 cells in total, proportioning 12.34%.
source: neutrophils (12,586 cells in total, proportioning 12.34%, marked with CSF3R)
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing cell type composition.

claim: ADC exhibited a significantly higher proportion of neutrophils than SCC (20.05% vs 4.23%).
source: According to our scRNA-seq data, ADC exhibited a significant higher proportion of neutrophils than SCC (20.05% vs 4.23%).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing comparative analysis.

claim: The proportion of T cells was higher in ADC (41.13%) compared to SCC (35.48%).
source: The proportion of T cells was also higher in ADC (41.13%) compared to SCC (35.48%).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing comparative analysis.

claim: SCC showed a nearly threefold enrichment of epithelial cell (47.43%) compared to ADC (16.48%).
source: Conversely, SCC showed a nearly threefold enrichment of epithelial cell (47.43%) compared to ADC (16.48%) (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 1F.

claim: Epithelial cells were classified into 12 sub-clusters based on differently expressed genes.
source: In order to explore the characteristics of these epithelial cells within the TIME of ADC, we further classified them into 12 sub-clusters based on the subsets of differently expressed genes (DEGs) in each group (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 2A.

claim: Epi_09_SST, Epi_10_CYSTM1, Epi_11_REG1A, and Epi_12_RRAD seemed to be exclusively enriched in ADC, not in SCC.
source: Notably, Epi_09_SST, Epi_10_CYSTM1, Epi_11_REG1A, and Epi_12_RRAD seemed to be exclusively enriched in ADC, not in SCC (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 2D.

claim: The sub-cluster Epi_10_CYSTM1 was exclusively present in stage IIIC patients.
source: Surprisingly, we found that the sub-cluster Epi_10_CYSTM1 was exclusively present in stage IIIC patients, indicating that it might be a potential target for identification of the biomarkers for late-stage patients (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cluster Epi_10_CYSTM1 was predicted to exhibit the highest degree of malignancy compared to other clusters.
source: In addition, we performed the malignancy scoring analysis, which demonstrated that cluster Epi_10_CYSTM1 was predicted to exhibit the highest degree of malignancy compared to other clusters (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 2F.

claim: Cluster Epi_10_CYSTM1 tended to be more active in regulating immunity-related pathways.
source: The results revealed that cluster Epi_10_CYSTM1 tended to be more active in regulating immunity-related pathways, which indicated this cluster might be possibly associated with dysfunction of immunity.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing GOBP analysis results.

claim: Cluster Epi_10_CYSTM1 was predicted to be more active in regulating cell-to-cell interaction.
source: In addition, cluster Epi_10_CYSTM1 was predicted to be more active in regulating cell-to-cell interaction (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 2G.

claim: SLC26A3 was specifically enriched in Epi_10_CYSTM1 cluster.
source: On the other hand, SLC26A3, ORM1, and ORM2 were specifically enriched in Epi_10_CYSTM1 and could be considered as potential candidate biomarkers for representation of this cluster.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing marker gene analysis.

claim: ADC patients at stage IIIC exhibited a higher expression of SLC26A3 compared to early stages.
source: The IHC staining further confirmed that ADC patients at stage IIIC exhibited a higher expression of SLC26A3 compared to early stages (FIGO stages I–II).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing IHC validation results.

claim: SLC26A3 might serve as a potential predictor of lymph node metastasis in ADC patients.
source: Furthermore, we tested on biopsy samples and it implied that SLC26A3 might serve as a potential predictor of LN metastasis.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing the potential clinical utility of SLC26A3.

claim: The upstaging rate for Cohort 1 was 10.85% (23 out of 212).
source: The rates of upstaging for each center are 10.85% (23 out of 212 in Cohort 1) and 15.31% (214 out of 1398 in Cohort 2), respectively.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing clinical cohort data.

claim: The upstaging rate for Cohort 2 was 15.31% (214 out of 1398).
source: The rates of upstaging for each center are 10.85% (23 out of 212 in Cohort 1) and 15.31% (214 out of 1398 in Cohort 2), respectively.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing clinical cohort data.

claim: The misdiagnose rate was significantly higher in HPV-negative patients than HPV-positive patients.
source: Interestingly, both cohorts of data revealed that the misdiagnose rate was significantly higher in HPV-negative patients than HPV-positive patients, especially among ADC patients.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing clinical cohort analysis.

claim: ADC patients were more likely to be misdiagnosed for clinical staging.
source: From the data of Cohort 2, it was observed that ADC patients were more likely to be misdiagnosed, which means that metastatic LNs were more difficult to detect in ADC patients via radiological tools.
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text describing clinical cohort analysis.

claim: A total of 52,297 T cells were categorized into eight main clusters.
source: A total of 52,297 T cells were categorized into eight main clusters (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 4A.

claim: T cells were re-clustered as exhausted T cells, cytotoxic T cells, regulatory T cells, and activated T cells.
source: Based on canonical genes (Li et al., 2022), these cells were re-clustered as the following four types of T cells: exhausted T cells (marked with CD8, TIGIT, PDCD1, LAG3, HAVCR2), cytotoxic T cells (marked with CD8 and CD3), regulatory T cells (Treg, marked with CD4, FOXP3, and IL2RA), and activated T cells (marked with CD8, C69, and CD3G) (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 4A–C.

claim: ADC had a significantly higher proportion of Tregs compared to SCC.
source: It was demonstrated that ADC had a significantly higher proportion of Tregs compared to SCC (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 4E.

claim: A total of 12,586 neutrophils were detected.
source: A total of 12,586 neutrophils were detected and the composition proportion in ADC (20.05%) was almost five times higher than that in SCC (4.23%) (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 1F.

claim: Neutrophils were initially grouped into six clusters based on gene expression modules.
source: All the cells were initially grouped into six clusters based on the gene expression modules (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 5A.

claim: Neutrophils were further clustered into three sub-types of TANs: pro-tumor TANs, anti-tumor TANs, and TANs with isg.
source: Based on the consensus markers identified by Jaillon et al., 2020 and Xue et al., 2022, we performed further clustering of the neutrophils in our dataset, resulting in the identification of three sub-types of TANs: pro-tumor TANs (Neu_03, marked with CD66, CD11, and MT1X), anti-tumor TANs (Neu_02, marked with CD66, CD11, CCL5, KRT5, and ELF3), TANs with isg (interferon-stimulated genes), and other undefined types (Neu_01, distinguished by CD66, CD11, IFITM2, S100A8, and LST1) (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 5B and C.

claim: The presence of pro-tumor TANs was significantly higher in ADC compared to SCC.
source: Notably, the presence of pro-tumor TANs was significantly higher in ADC compared to SCC (Figure 5D), as well as in HPV-negative cases compared to HPV-positive cases (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 5D.

claim: The proportion of anti-tumor TANs in ADC was predominantly lower than that in SCC.
source: On the other hand, the proportion of anti-tumor TANs in ADC was predominantly lower than that in SCC (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 5D.

claim: Patients with higher expression of gene panels specific to pro-tumor TANs exhibited a poorer prognosis.
source: The patients with higher expression of gene panels specific to pro-tumor TANs exhibited a poorer prognosis compared to those with lower expression (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 5F.

claim: Six distinctive clusters of plasma/B cells were identified.
source: In our study, we identified six distinctive clusters of plasma/B cells based on the set of gene enrichment: Plasma/B_01 (marked with IGHA2, IGHG2, and IGLC2), Plasma/B_02 (marked with HLA-DRA, HLA-DPB, and CD37), Plasma/B_03 (marked with KRT17 and S100A2), Plasma/B_04 (marked with CCL5, CXCL13, IL-32, and CCL4), Plasma/B_05 (marked with CXCL8), and Plasma/B_06 (marked with HMGB2) (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 6A–C.

claim: The proportion of Plasma/B_01_IGHA2 was found to be higher in ADC compared to SCC.
source: Interestingly, the proportion of Plasma/B_01_IGHA2 was found to be higher in ADC compared to SCC, and it was also slightly higher in HPV-negative cases than in HPV-positive cases (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 6D.

claim: Higher expression of Plasma/B_01_IGHA2 signature genes predicted a poorer prognosis of CC patients.
source: When we combined the top 50 signature genes in Plasma/B_01_IGHA2-enriched subset and performed the survival analysis using TCGA database, we observed that higher expression of the signature genes predicted a poorer prognosis of CC patients (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 6E.

claim: ADC-enriched epithelial sub-clusters exhibited a higher propensity for interaction with Tregs through ALCAM and MHC-II signaling pathways.
source: Firstly, in comparison to SCC, ADC-enriched epithelial sub-clusters exhibited a higher propensity for interaction with Tregs through ligand-receptor signaling pathways, including ALCAM (ALCAM>>CD6) and MHC-II (HLA-DR>>CD4) (Figure 7A–E)
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 7A–E.

claim: The interaction of TGFβ>>TGFBR between Tregs and epithelial cells was activated in ADC but not in SCC.
source: Interestingly, the CellChat analysis revealed that, compared to other pathways, such as CD46>>JAG1 and GZMA>>PARD3, the interaction of TGFβ>>TGFBR between Tregs and epithelial cells (particularly in cluster Epi_10_CYSTM1) was activated in ADC but not in SCC (Figure 7F and G).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 7F and G.

claim: A greater recruitment of Tregs was observed in close proximity to regions exhibiting high SLC26A3 expression.
source: To test these hypotheses, we conducted immunofluorescence (IF) analysis and observed a greater recruitment of Tregs (marked by FOXP3) in close proximity to regions exhibiting high SLC26A3 expression (Epi_10_CYSTM1 cell cluster) (Figure 7H).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 7H.

claim: Tumors displaying high SLC26A3 levels exhibited significantly increased expression of ALDH1A1.
source: Furthermore, when compared to regions with low SLC26A3 expression, tumors displaying high SLC26A3 levels exhibited significantly increased expression of Aldehyde Dehydrogenase 1 Family Member A1 (ALDH1A1), a known marker for cancer stem cells in CC (Douville et al., 2009; Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: SLC26A3high tumor cells expressing ALCAM were identified in close proximity to CD6+Tregs.
source: Notably, we identified SLC26A3high tumor cells expressing ALCAM in close proximity to CD6+Tregs, suggesting potential involvement of ALCAM>>CD6 signaling in Treg recruitment (Figure 7I).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 7I.

claim: Reduced E-cadherin expression was observed in tumor cells within SLC26A3high regions.
source: Additionally, we observed reduced E-cadherin expression in tumor cells within SLC26A3high regions, possibly induced by TGFβ secreted by adjacent Tregs (Figure 7J, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the manuscript text and references Figure 7J.

claim: The 5-year survival rate for early-stage cervical cancer patients exceeds 90%.
source: When diagnosed at early stages, the 5-year survival rate for CC patients exceeds 90%, surpassing that of other gynecologic malignancies (Gennigens et al., 2022; Schiffman et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gennigens et al., 2022 and Schiffman et al., 2007.

claim: If cervical cancer metastasizes to lymph nodes, the survival rate decreases to 30–60%.
source: However, if CC metastasizes to the intraperitoneal or retroperitoneal LNs, the survival rate will decrease to 30–60% (Cohen et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cohen et al., 2019.

claim: The 5-year survival rate for recurrent cervical cancer patients is less than 20%.
source: Worse still, the 5-year survival rate for recurrent CC patients is less than 20% (Li et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2016.

claim: TGFβ is a canonical secreted protein that induces carcinogenesis.
source: TGFβ is a canonical secreted protein that induces carcinogenesis, such as cancer cell proliferation, invasion, self-renewal, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Derynck et al., 2021; Massagué, 2008; Tauriello et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Derynck et al., 2021, Massagué, 2008, and Tauriello et al., 2022.

claim: ALCAM and MHC-II signaling pathways are essential for Treg recruitment, expansion, and stabilization to establish the immunosuppressive microenvironment.
source: Firstly, in comparison to SCC, ADC-enriched epithelial sub-clusters exhibited a higher propensity for interaction with Tregs through ligand-receptor signaling pathways, including ALCAM (ALCAM>>CD6) and MHC-II (HLA-DR>>CD4) (Figure 7A–E), which have been reported to be essential for Treg recruitment, expansion, and stabilization to establish the immunosuppressive microenvironment (Chalmers et al., 2022; Ferragut et al., 2021; Freitas et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chalmers et al., 2022, Ferragut et al., 2021, and Freitas et al., 2019.

claim: Pro-tumor TANs are characterized by CD66, CD11, CD170, and PD-L1.
source: It has been clearly investigated that pro-tumor TANs, characterized by CD66, CD11, CD170, and PD-L1, exert the oncogenic roles by promoting tumor cell proliferation, angiogenesis, inducing genetic instability, and most importantly causing immunosuppression (Jaillon et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jaillon et al., 2020.

claim: ALDH1A1 is a known marker for cancer stem cells in cervical cancer.
source: Furthermore, when compared to regions with low SLC26A3 expression, tumors displaying high SLC26A3 levels exhibited significantly increased expression of Aldehyde Dehydrogenase 1 Family Member A1 (ALDH1A1), a known marker for cancer stem cells in CC (Douville et al., 2009; Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Douville et al., 2009.

claim: The ANNEXIN pathway can promote the chemotaxis of neutrophils.
source: Previous studies have reported that the ANNEXIN pathway can promote the chemotaxis of neutrophils (Araújo et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Araújo et al., 2021.

claim: Tumor cells acquire higher stemness present more aggressive features of resistance to immunotherapy.
source: It has also been widely reported that tumor cells acquire higher stemness present more aggressive features of resistance to immunotherapy (Dianat-Moghadam et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dianat-Moghadam et al., 2022.

claim: Immunotherapies are less effective in ADC patients, especially those who are not infected with HPV.
source: It has been reported that immunotherapies are less effective in ADC patients, especially those who are not infected with HPV (Attademo et al., 2020; Ferrall et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Attademo et al., 2020 and Ferrall et al., 2021.

claim: The recruited Tregs might secrete TGFβ to stimulate the tumor epithelial cells of ADC, leading to increased stemness.
source: Thus, we speculate that the recruited Tregs might secrete TGFβ to stimulate the tumor epithelial cells of ADC, leading to increased stemness.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from CellChat analysis and known TGFβ functions.

claim: The establishment of an immunosuppressive TIME in ADC may involve the recruitment of regulatory T cells to the tumor area.
source: These findings lead us to hypothesize that the establishment of an immunosuppressive TIME in ADC may involve the recruitment of regulatory T cells (Tregs) to the tumor area and the subsequent inactivation of a substantial proportion of cytotoxic T cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from T cell analysis results.

claim: ADC-specific epithelial cell sub-clusters may actively engage in the recruitment of pro-tumor TANs.
source: This suggests that ADC-specific epithelial cell sub-clusters may actively engage in the recruitment of pro-tumor TANs.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from neutrophil enrichment data.

claim: The increased malignancy observed in ADC may be related to the enrichment of pro-tumor TANs.
source: These findings suggest that the increased malignancy observed in ADC, particularly in HPV-negative cases, may also be related to the enrichment of pro-tumor TANs.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from pro-tumor TAN analysis and survival data.

claim: The intricate crosstalk between the Epi_10_CYSTM1 cell cluster and Tregs might help to establish an immunosuppressive TIME.
source: Altogether, these findings confirm the intricate crosstalk between the Epi_10_CYSTM1 cell cluster and Tregs, which might help to establish an immunosuppressive TIME and sustain heightened stemness in tumor cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from CellChat analysis and immunofluorescence validation.

claim: The infiltration of a large number of Tregs in ADC may significantly accelerate immune evasion.
source: The infiltration of a large number of Tregs in ADC may significantly accelerate immune evasion (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from Treg enrichment data and known Treg functions.

claim: The presence of a higher number of Tregs infiltrating the tumor area of ADC may partially explain the increased resistance to immunotherapy.
source: Therefore, the presence of a higher number of Tregs infiltrating the tumor area of ADC may partially explain the increased resistance to immunotherapy.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from Treg enrichment data and known immunotherapy resistance mechanisms.
